business.description: Dish TV India Limited is a Direct-to-Home (DTH) service provider that is repositioning into a hybrid entertainment ecosystem offering DTH, OTT streaming (Watcho), smart TVs (VZY), e-commerce (ShopZop), and content aggregation (Content India).

outlook.statement: Confident that new initiatives (VZY TV, Watcho, hybrid packages, ShopZop, Content India) will drive recovery and growth; aims to lead transition from set-top boxes to smart screens in India's media distribution landscape.
The Company continues to diversify its revenue streams and product-mix, besides taking strong cost optimization measures towards sustainable revenue growth.
The Company does not anticipate that SCN will have any material adverse impact.
Going forward, the Company will continue to deploy its resources, capabilities and strategies towards creating and safeguarding long-term value for its stakeholders.

FICCI-EY report projects TV reach to cross 200 million households by 2028 and linear TV revenue to fall by 5% until 2028. CTV reach expected to reach 83 million households by end of five years and ad revenue growth of 18% to reach ₹ 164 billion by 2028. Pay TV to compete with digital, OTT and social media platforms, while FTA channels will deepen for 53 million Free TV households. Integration of Pay TV and broadband services will accelerate bundled offerings.
Dish TV aims to capture substantial revenue from non-DTH businesses by 2027. Segments hold a bright future and promise to confidently drive better performance in the forthcoming period.
Watcho, VZY and Zing brands stay strong with FLIQS and a blend of FTA and Pay TV, while ShopZop remains popular with businesses.
Company continues to adopt and leverage technology and deliver seamless entertainment experiences through its offerings.
positive business outlook, cash generation capability

management believes that it is appropriate to prepare the consolidated financial statements on a going concern basis considering sufficient operational cash flow, no debt in books, positive business outlook, cash generation capability

Salary risk: Actual salary increases will increase the Plan's liability.
Investment risk: Assets liabilities mismatch and actual investment return on assets lower than the discount rate assumed at the last valuation date can impact the liability.
Discount rate risk: Reduction in discount rate in subsequent valuations can increase the plan's liability.
Mortality risk: Actual deaths and disability cases proving lower or higher than assumed in the valuation can impact the liabilities.
Withdrawals risk: Actual withdrawals proving higher or lower than assumed withdrawals and change of withdrawal rates at subsequent valuations can impact plan's liability.
Credit risk: The Group's exposure to credit risk is influenced mainly by cash and cash equivalents, trade receivables and financial assets measured at amortised cost.
Liquidity risk: The risk that suitable sources of funding for the Group's business activities may not be available.
Foreign currency risk: The Group has international transactions/balances and is exposed to foreign exchange risk arising from foreign currency transactions.
Price risk: The exposure to price risk arises from investments held by the Group and classified in the balance sheet either as fair value through OCI or at fair value through profit or loss.
